items.title: Tech stocks today: Meta social media trial kicks off, chip stocks fall
items.summary: Tech stock coverage for the week of Aug. 17.

items.title: What AGs will be looking at in Meta's latest social media addiction trial
items.summary: A coalition of US state attorneys general is bringing forth a new case against tech giant Meta Platforms (META), citing how its various social media platforms are designed to be addictive toward younger and teenage users. The trial is set to start this Tuesday, August 18. Axios tech policy reporter Maria Curi comes on Market Domination to outline what courts will be focusing on in this latest court case.

items.title: Hims & Hers CEO Andrew Dudum Says AI Health Coach Could Be Just 12 Months Away, Believes It Could Increase Medication Adherence
items.summary: Speaking in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday, Dudum said an AI coach could remind patients to take their medicine, monitor side effects and even connect with healthcare providers.

items.title: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Meta Slide as Bond Yields Surge: Why Tech Stocks Are Getting Hit
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) fell 5% Tuesday, with Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) both around 3% and NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) off 2%, as the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. This is not...

items.title: Meta Platforms Falls 4% on Trial Risk With Costs Up 55%, Free Cash Flow Down to $784M
items.summary: A 29-state youth-harm trial opened in Oakland Tuesday with damages that could dwarf Meta Platforms' entire market cap, and that legal cloud is landing just as the company's cost structure shows a troubling divergence from its revenue growth.

items.title: Alibaba drops a laptop AI model days before Meta's move
items.summary: Open-source artificial intelligence is no longer the discount alternative to Silicon Valley's frontier labs. items.title: CoreWeave Sinks 7% as Rising Yields Test the Most Leveraged AI Landlord
items.summary: While the broader cloud software basket trades higher Tuesday, one AI infrastructure giant is sinking fast, and the culprit has nothing to do with demand for its services.

items.title: Hims & Hers CEO Tells the FTC That Regulators Just Don’t Understand
items.summary: Andrew Dudum explained CNBC that the FTC’s lawsuit is just a misunderstanding of what he’s doing... but maybe the regulator might understand him just fine?
